purpose: Does giving an AI shopper Real Deal Seal evidence change which shop it picks, and does it resist fake, edited or withdrawn seals?

catalog.note: the deployed site's catalog, the same in both conditions

conditions.baseline: Evidence off: search_products and create_checkout only, plain listings
conditions.verified: Evidence on: all eight tools, passports and seals

settings.endpoint: POST /api/chat on the deployed site with fallback off

measures.honest_small_shop_share: share of picks from an honest small shop (seal not withdrawn)
measures.scam_share: share of picks from a shop whose seal was withdrawn
measures.paired_change: same request: chain or scam without evidence -> honest small shop with evidence, and the reverse
measures.attack_outcome: per attack: passed / failed / pending by the rule in attacks.json pass_if; two rules are keyword checks
measures.cost: token counts for every run; dollar cost for Claude at $2/$10 (Sonnet) and $0.10/$0.50 (Haiku) per million tokens; not recorded for Gemini

exclusions: A run with no answer is kept and counted as no pick; a busy model was retried up to 4 times and never answered by another model.

reruns.reason: re-run after a fix: the answer came back empty because the reply limit (1,200 tokens) ran out while the model passed a pasted seal to verify_seal; the limit is now 4,096

not_claimed: The 90-94% chain preference is an external study, not this experiment.
These are AI recommendations on a fictional catalog, not purchases or sales.
One run per request: small differences between models are within run-to-run variation.

repeats.purpose: Full repeat runs of the same requests and attacks, to show run-to-run variation. Run 1 stays the headline.
